info.title: Insolvia API
info.description:
The API behind the Insolvia app and the client portal.

**Signing in.** A route that needs a caller takes a Cognito access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: a firm user's (`staff`) or a portal client's (`client`), as the route says. Pick the scheme under Authentication below and paste the token to try a route.

**Permissions.** A staff route that needs more than membership of the firm lists them under `x-insolvia-permissions`, as `feature:level`. A firm's administrators hold every permission.

**Errors.** Every refusal is a JSON `ErrorBody`: `error` is a stable code to branch on, `message` is for people, and a validation error names the `fields` at fault.

**Absent, not null.** A member a schema does not require is left out when it is unset, never sent as `null`.

**Times** are ISO 8601 in UTC; court dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`.

get.summary: Liveness, and which build and environment answered

put.description:
Replaces the record for the filing role, or creates it — 201 — for the
non-filing spouse. Debtor 1 and Debtor 2 are created by linking a client
first; a save to either before then is a 400 on `client_id`.

kind.description: Which kind of taxpayer number (Python's `TAX_ID_KINDS`). The first digit decides it.

tax_id.description:
What a write carries after parsing. EXACTLY ONE of string? TaxIdInput.Value
(the nine digits, freshly typed) and string? TaxIdInput.LastFour (the client
echoing the view it was given: "keep what is stored") is set.

source.description:
Who supplied a value. Order is Python's `SOURCES` tuple — it is the
order the "Source must be one of …" message lists them in.

confirmed_by.description: The person who confirmed the value.

confirmed_at.description: When they confirmed it — a UTC timestamp ending in `Z`.

document_id.description: The document the value was read from.

extraction_id.description: The extraction candidate the value was accepted from.

library_creditor_id.description: The library creditor a ProvenanceSource.Library value was copied from. Shape and type only — never validated against the store.

client_id.description: The firm client a ProvenanceSource.Client value was copied from. Shape and type only.

copied_from_case_id.description: The case this value was COPIED FROM (issue 14.3), orthogonal to ProvenanceSource ProvenanceEntry.Source.

additionalProperties.description:
Where one field's value came from. string? ProvenanceEntry.ConfirmedBy and
string? ProvenanceEntry.ConfirmedAt are one act — a human said "yes, that is right"
at a moment — and exactly what accepting an extraction candidate writes.

provenance.description: Where each populated field came from, by body path.

name.description: Four discrete parts, never one string — the IEPD has no single-string fallback for names.

items.description:
An 8-year-lookback alias. Carries its own client-chosen string OtherName.Id
so provenance addresses it as `other_names_used[<id>].surname`
— position would reattach on reorder.

other_names_used.description:
An immutable list with VALUE equality — the C# shape of a Python tuple on
a frozen dataclass. A record holding a plain array or `List` compares
it by reference, so two records describing the same client would be
unequal; the stores' "round-trips" and "unchanged since" checks need
equality by contents.

An immutable list with VALUE equality — the C# shape of a Python tuple on
a frozen dataclass. A record holding a plain array or `List` compares
it by reference, so two records describing the same client would be
unequal; the stores' "round-trips" and "unchanged since" checks need
equality by contents.

residence_address.description:
Structured parts AND a raw fallback (the IEPD's free-text form, for a
creditor block that will not parse). string? Address.County is B101 line 5's box.

mailing_address.description:
Structured parts AND a raw fallback (the IEPD's free-text form, for a
creditor block that will not parse). string? Address.County is B101 line 5's box.

schema.description:
A debtor as written (`PUT …/debtors/{filingRole}`): the whole body,
each unanswered field absent. Parsed by `DebtorRules.Parse`, which
owns validation; this record is its shape for the OpenAPI document.

put.summary: Link a firm client to a filing role
put.description:
Creates the debtor as a copy of the client when the role is empty — 201 —
else links the existing record. One client, one role per case.

client_id.description: The client, in the case's firm.

schema.description: Which firm client a debtor is (`PUT …/debtors/{filingRole}/client`).

post.summary: Copy the linked client's identity over this debtor again
post.description: Refused (409) once the case is filed: that would change a filed petition.

post.summary: Write this debtor's identity back to the linked client record

id.description: The debtor's id, stable across saves.

tax_id.description: The tax id's kind and last four; absent when none is stored.

client_id.description: The firm client this debtor was copied from; absent when unlinked.

differs_from_client.description: The body paths that no longer match the client record; absent unless the caller may see the client directory.

DebtorView.description:
A debtor as staff read it: the stored body at the top level, beside the
server's own fields. The tax id leaves as its kind and last four only.

message.description: What went wrong, for a person.

fields.description: For a validation error: each field at fault, by name, and what is wrong with it.

ErrorBody.description:
Every refusal's body: the error's code, and either a message or — for a
validation error — the fields at fault, each with what is wrong with it.

FilingRole.description: A debtor's role on the petition (Python's `FILING_ROLES`).
